globalIndexSpace.description: l0 occupies [0, l0Count); l1 occupies [l0Count, l0Count + l1Count). L2 chunks are disjoint from both and are not part of this space.

dequantization.magnitude: mag = magu / 16 - 2    (apparent V/VT magnitude; magu = round((mag + 2) * 16); step 0.0625 mag; representable range -2.000 .. +13.938)
dequantization.colourIndex: ci = ciu / 40 - 0.5    (colour index; ciu = round((ci + 0.5) * 40); step 0.025; representable range -0.500 .. +5.875)
dequantization.colourIndexBand: IMPORTANT: the stored colour index is NOT Johnson B-V for most stars. AT-HYG`s `ci` column is the Tycho BT-VT colour for every row whose mag_src is T, which is the large majority. Measured against HYG v4.1`s Johnson B-V over 106,941 cross-matched stars, the offset is colour dependent: about +0.00 at B-V 0.0, +0.02 at 0.45, +0.08 at 0.75, +0.18 at 1.05, +0.26 at 1.35, +0.32 at 1.75 and +0.50 beyond 2.0 — i.e. red stars are stored noticeably redder than their Johnson B-V. The 165 stars flagged 0x80 were back-filled from HYG v4.1 and ARE Johnson B-V. A renderer mapping colour index to temperature should either apply a BT-VT to B-V transformation or accept that K and M stars render somewhat too red.
dequantization.magnitudeBand: The stored apparent magnitude is AT-HYG`s `mag`, which for mag_src=T rows is the Tycho/Hipparcos band rather than Johnson V. Median offset against HYG v4.1 Johnson V over 107,336 cross-matched stars is +0.074 mag, reaching about +0.37 for the brightest stars (Sirius is stored as -1.088; its Johnson V is -1.44). Brightness ORDERING is essentially preserved, so brightest-first sorting and magnitude cuts remain valid, but the number should be labelled an instrumental magnitude, not V.
dequantization.absoluteMagnitude: absmag = mag - 5 * (log10(sqrt(x*x + y*y + z*z)) - 1)   — not stored; derive it from the dequantized mag and the position
dequantization.positionL0L1: float32 parsecs, stored verbatim — no quantization applied
dequantization.positionL2: x_pc = x_i16 * shell.scale, where shell.scale = shell.radiusPc / 32767 and a star`s shell is the manifest entry whose [start, start + count) index range contains it

flags.bit1 (0x02): has-exoplanet — host matched a NASA Exoplanet Archive pscomppars row
flags.bit2 (0x04): is-variable — HYG v4.1 `var` (variable-star designation) is non-empty for the HIP/HD-matched row
flags.bit3 (0x08): is-multiple — HYG v4.1 `base` non-empty or `comp` > 1 for the HIP/HD-matched row
flags.bit4 (0x10): ci-was-defaulted — AT-HYG `ci` was empty; the stored value is the solar default 0.65
flags.bit6 (0x40): absmag-missing — AT-HYG `absmag` was empty (derive it from mag + distance instead)
flags.bit7 (0x80): ci-from-hyg — AT-HYG had no colour index, so it was back-filled from HYG v4.1 (bit4 is then clear)

ingestStats.distanceSentinelNote: 89 stars carry AT-HYG's magic distance of exactly 100000 pc (parallax exactly 0.01000 mas), which the catalogue uses for "no usable parallax". They are real stars at an UNKNOWN distance, not measurements at 100 kpc: their implied absolute magnitudes are around -10 to -11, brighter than any real star. They are retained so the global index space stays stable, but a renderer should not treat their positions as measured, and an inspector should report their distance as unknown rather than as 100 kpc. Every other AT-HYG distance beyond 20 kpc is a distinct, irregular value; only this one repeats.
